prompt: The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an adverbial usage error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don’t find any error, select ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Mr. Narayanan / is a rather / lazy man.
explanation: 'Is a rather lazy man' is correct usage; 'rather' properly modifies the adjective 'lazy' after the article.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: Today she said to her friend, “You’re the sweetest person I have met ever”.
explanation: With the present perfect, 'ever' is placed before the past participle: 'I have ever met'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: As is usual with stories of this genre, / in spite of their varying socio political realities, / the youngsters have fallen in love / with each other madly.
options: the youngsters have fallen in love
in spite of their varying socio political realities
As is usual with stories of this genre
explanation: The adverb belongs with the verb phrase: 'have fallen madly in love with each other', not 'with each other madly'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The child was irritable / because she had not / soundly slept / the previous night.
explanation: The adverb of manner follows the verb: 'had not slept soundly'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. He always stood up for the rights of the oppressed. /No error
explanation: 'Stood up for' is the correct phrasal verb and 'the oppressed' correctly uses 'the + adjective' for a class of people, so the sentence is correct.

prompt: Read the sentence given below and identify if there is an error in it. The error can be in any segment of the sentence which are marked A, B, C, and D. Select option D if there is 'No error'. (A) Ritika angrily / (B) spoke to Kartik / (C) after the meeting / (D) No error.
explanation: An adverb of manner should follow the verb/object, so 'Ritika angrily' is wrong; it should be 'Ritika spoke angrily to Kartik'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Maria was unhappy / because she terribly performed / in the examination / conducted last month.
explanation: The adverb of manner should follow the verb: 'because she performed terribly'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Before the internet was available on mobile, I read often books for entertainment and information.
explanation: The adverb of frequency 'often' must not separate the verb from its object; correct order is 'I often read books'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Rahul speaks fluently English / although he makes / quite a lot of mistakes /while writing.
explanation: An adverb of manner should not come between the verb and its object; it should be 'Rahul speaks English fluently'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.
sentence: He sing always when he is having a shower.
explanation: Adverbs of frequency like 'always' come between the subject and the main verb, and the third-person singular needs '-s': 'He always sings'.

prompt: Identify the best way to improve the underlined part of the given sentence. If there is
sentence: no improvement required, select ‘no improvement’- I am like very much Chinese food and have learnt to cook it.
options: am liking very much Chinese food
explanation: 'Like' is a stative verb used without 'am', and the adverbial phrase 'very much' must follow the object: 'like Chinese food very much'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: She finished her quickly breakfast and rushed to school.
explanation: The adverb 'quickly' must not split the verb from its object; it follows the object: 'finished her breakfast quickly'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: He takes his always dog for a walk in the park.
options: takes his dog for always a walk
takes his dog for an always walk
always takes his dog for a walk
his dog for a walk always takes
explanation: The adverb of frequency 'always' comes before the main verb: 'always takes his dog for a walk'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: Suman performed at the festival well yesterday.
explanation: Adverb order is manner–place–time, giving 'performed well at the festival yesterday'.
